page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance is positioned for low-intensity workloads. In CPU testing, the stress-ng single-core score of 1101.98 and multi-core score of 1451.88 fall into the bottom 25% and 10% of benchmarked servers, respectively. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached read and write large-block bandwidths measured at 12.0 GB/sec and 10.51 GB/sec. The Geekbench single-core score of 841.0 and multi-core score of 1028.0 reflect limited computational throughput, while Redis SET operations reach 1.33 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-2 provides a high memory capacity relative to its processing power, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications that do not require high CPU performance. The tradeoff involves lower computational speed and memory bandwidth in exchange for a larger memory footprint. This profile is suitable for lightweight database operations, caching layers, basic web serving with a static throughput of 1.43 GB/sec, and small-scale language model inference, where prompt processing and text generation for a 135M model achieve 133.75 and 61.66 tokens per second respectively.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-CPU ratio without intensive processing needs. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results place its computational and memory bandwidth performance in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1101.98 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 12.0 GB/sec. Qualitatively, it offers a cost-effective solution for memory-heavy, compute-light tasks. It is best suited for lightweight databases, caching systems like Redis, basic web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
